objective: Rewrite the chkdsk front end on rune (https://github.com/anomalyco/rune), replacing the r3bl_tui terminal UI with an elegant, simple, performant native rune window while keeping the app's behavior.
scope: Work only in the git worktree /home/user/chkdsk-rune (branch rune-rewrite). The app: Windows disk-health dashboard in Rust, pt_BR UI. Modules: src/backend.rs (Windows IOCTL/SMART/NVMe queries via windows-sys), src/health.rs (heuristic score), src/history.rs (%APPDATA%\chkdsk\historico.json, ETA), src/model.rs, src/parse.rs, src/ui.rs (1916-line r3bl_tui UI), src/main.rs; README.md documents behavior and controls

Rune facts (from research, verify against the repo): Rust GPU UI framework (wgpu+winit), MIT, no crates.io release; depend as rune = { git = "https://github.com/anomalyco/rune", rev = "<pinned dev commit>" } and pin an exact rev; rune-kit crate in the same repo has TabStrip, SegmentedControl, Sidebar, Badge, Progress, shell, SplitView. Entry: rune::run(AppSpec::new(title,(w,h),State::default,view)); view(&State,&mut Cx)->El built from col()/row()/text(); handlers .on_press(|s:&mut State|..); AppSpec::setup(state,wake) gives a Waker; poll(state,clock,tx)->bool with tx.wake_after(Duration); App::new(spec).init(..), app.handle() gives Send+Sync AppHandle::update(|s,tx|..) to push state from background threads; AppSpec::on_key for window keys; .scroll(ScrollSpec{..}), .virtualize; tok::theme(true); headless testing via Runtime::new(state,view,(w,h),Env{system_dark:true,scale:2.0}), rt.frame(dt), rt.find(key), rt.pointer_down/up; headless snapshots via -- --snap out.png --scene name and --tree. Read crates/rune/README.md, crates/rune-kit/README.md, AGENTS.md and examples (hello, live-values, todo, kit-gallery) in the rune repo (clone it to a temp dir outside the repo, e.g. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-chkdsk/6d301693-1f05-56b7-955a-cbe3996284b5/scratchpad/rune-src) before designing

Current behavior to keep (read src/ui.rs for exact strings): a list/tabs of disks to switch between; per-disk panel with status badge (SAUDÁVEL / ATENÇÃO / INDISPONÍVEL), 0-100 score, Vida estimada (ETA), Desgaste, Temperatura, Tempo ligado, Última leitura, raw ATA attributes, status/error messages (e.g. Permissão insuficiente…); discovery every 15s, max 4 concurrent queries, background collection that never blocks the UI; keyboard: Left/Right and Tab/Shift+Tab switch disks, Up/Down scroll the panel, q and Esc quit; mouse: click a disk to select, wheel scrolls; color semantics of the palette in ui.rs:29-68 (healthy/attention/unknown)
constraints: Keep backend.rs, health.rs, history.rs, model.rs, parse.rs behavior and their tests unchanged except for the minimal edits rune integration needs; the rewrite is of the UI layer and main.rs, so the scoring, history and telemetry stay exactly as they are

Make the crate build and its tests run on Linux as well as Windows: gate the Windows-only backend with cfg(windows) and give non-Windows a stub that reports no disks (replace the main.rs compile_error), so UI logic is testable headless here; the Windows build stays the shipped product and the Windows targets (x86_64, aarch64, i686 msvc) must keep compiling — verify with cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (install the target with rustup if missing; use cargo xwin only if plain check cannot work) and name any target you could not verify
Use #![cfg_attr(windows, windows_subsystem = "windows")] or equivalent so no console window opens on Windows, unless rune docs say otherwise

Remove r3bl_tui and any dependency only it needed; keep the dependency set minimal (rune, rune-kit if used, serde, serde_json, windows-sys); drop tokio if a std::thread collector with AppHandle::update is simpler
